So here's the funny thing about carbs: your body runs on them. They're basically your primary fuel source. All of your muscles including your brain run on carbs. They're also pretty damn important for your immune system. And here's the thing about excess carbs: they get stored as muscle glycogen over fat. That's right. If you eat lots of carbs, they go to your muscles first, then fat. The conversion of carbs to fat is actually really inefficient.

Then there's fat. Fat gets stored pretty damn efficiently as... drum roll please...

...

fat. That means if you eat fat, you get fat.

And the other thing about fat is that your body won't ordinarily burn it unless it doesn't have a lot of carbs to go after. That's why a ketogenic diet restricts your carbs. It's forcing your body to use fat instead of carbs.

Another thing about carbs: simple carbs come without fiber and nutrients and will therefore digest rapidly and spike your blood sugar, leading to an insulin spike which clears your blood, which in turn causes a craving for more food. Complex carbs don't really cause this issue.

So enjoy your carbs. They're not evil. Just avoid simple carbs and you'll be fine. Oh, and getting enough protein isn't an issue. That's a myth.

Next time the ham planet tells you about the evils of carbs and the awesomeness of fat, try explaining all this to him and enjoy his reaction. It might be interesting.
